title: Advice to young musicians
summary: Practice, meet good people, and let young players sit in.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: What kind of advice would you give to young musicians just getting started that have ideas of finding their way or seeking their fame and fortune in the music business?
You're talking about the ones that are just coming up?

In other words, besides, what you remember I was saying about my practice. That's what I was thinking. Practice. [Laughs] Well, that's one of the big things. Then, get around with, go around and listen and hear and meet the good people in the business that like to talk. I met some nice young musicians since I've been here. You know, and I let

some sit in with me. They've been back and forth. They're like, from far back like Cleveland, all around, while they in school. If I find out they can play, I bring them in and they sit right in with me. And, some of them can play nice. And I would say do more of that.
And besides practicing all the time, they'll move on until they meet the right people. You know, cause I like to see a young musician play.
